stories.headline: Ukrainian drones hit St. Petersburg oil terminal, Kronstadt naval base, Tambov plant in deep strike

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian long-range drones struck the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal on June 3, flying more than 1,000 km to hit one of Russia's largest oil transshipment hubs in the Baltic region
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian long-range drones struck an oil terminal in St. Petersburg and set it ablaze, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Wednesday... The drones flew more than 1,000 kilometres (600 miles) to hit the terminal in Russia's second-largest city

key_facts.fact: The strikes hit on the opening day of the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF), Russia's flagship event for attracting foreign capital, with Putin scheduled to address it Friday
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine has carried out a strike on the outskirts of Russia's St Petersburg, hours before the opening of a major economic forum designed to attract foreign investment into the country... Thousands of guests from 130 countries are due to attend

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces set fire to the Russian guided-missile corvette Boikiy in dry dock at the Kronstadt naval base, the main stronghold of Russia's Baltic Fleet
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) hit a Russian warship armed with missiles at the Kronstadt naval base in Russia's Leningrad Oblast on June 3... drones 'tracked down and set fire' to the corvette Boikyi, which is armed with guided missiles

key_facts.fact: Drones also hit the Progress plant in Michurinsk, Tambov region, 600 km from the front line, which produces aviation and missile control equipment for Russia's military
key_facts.excerpt: The third confirmed target was a defense-industrial facility in Russia's Tambov region involved in weapons production. Zelenskyy said the site was nearly 600 kilometers from the front line. According to Russian outlet ASTRA, the target was the Progress plant

key_facts.fact: Russia fired 198 long-range drones at Ukraine overnight; Ukraine's air force neutralized 189
key_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile, Russia fired 198 long-range drones at Ukraine last night, according to Ukraine's air force, with air defenses neutralizing 189.

key_facts.fact: Local authorities reported 59 drones shot down overnight; three districts of St. Petersburg were hit; the city's airport briefly suspended flights and mobile internet was cut
key_facts.excerpt: Local authorities said air defences shot down 59 drones overnight and that three different districts of St Petersburg had been hit, although no one was killed.

stories.headline: Iran drone hits Kuwait airport killing one; FM Araghchi says peace talks made 'no tangible progress'

key_facts.fact: An Iranian drone strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one person and wounded 63, damaging a passenger terminal that had reopened only on Monday after months of war-related closure
key_facts.excerpt: Kuwaiti officials said an Iranian drone strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one person and wounded 63

key_facts.fact: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said negotiations to end the war have made 'no tangible progress' and warned an Israeli attack on Beirut would trigger a 'full-scale resumption' of the conflict
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's foreign minister said Wednesday that 'no tangible progress' has been made in negotiations to end the Middle East war as fresh US and Iranian strikes strained a fragile ceasefire

key_facts.fact: US CENTCOM said an additional wave of Iranian drones tried to target US forces in Kuwait but failed, and dismissed as false IRGC claims that Iranian missiles hit the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain
key_facts.excerpt: CENTCOM said an 'additional wave of Iranian drones' attempted to target US forces in Kuwait, but the attack was unsuccessful... CENTCOM dismissed IRGC claims that Iranian missiles and drones had struck the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain

key_facts.fact: Hezbollah said it launched 13 attacks against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon on Wednesday targeting troop gatherings, military vehicles and army command posts
key_facts.excerpt: Hezbollah said on Wednesday it launched 13 attacks against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, targeting troop gatherings, military vehicles and army command posts

key_facts.fact: Oil prices rose more than 2% on the renewed Gulf hostilities; the Strait of Hormuz, which previously handled about a fifth of global oil and LNG shipments, remains largely closed more than three months after the US-Israeli strikes on Iran
key_facts.excerpt: The attacks are the latest to test a shaky ceasefire, sending oil prices up more than 2%, as the strait remains largely closed more than three months after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran

key_facts.fact: Israeli drone strikes killed at least six people in southern Lebanon on Wednesday and targeted a car just south of Beirut, the closest strike to the Lebanese capital since a US-mediated partial ceasefire announced Monday
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli drone strikes killed at least six people in southern Lebanon and targeted a car just south of Beirut, Lebanese security sources said... the attack on the car appeared to mark the closest attack to Beirut since Trump asked Israel not to hit the Lebanese capital

stories.headline: US private payrolls jumped 122,000 in May, ADP's strongest reading since January 2025

key_facts.fact: ADP reported private employers added 122,000 jobs in May, above the Dow Jones consensus of 110,000 and the largest gain since January 2025
key_facts.excerpt: ADP reported said companies added 122,000 workers in May, up from 105,000 in April and better than the Dow Jones consensus estimate for 110,000... May marked the strongest month since January 2025

key_facts.fact: Eight of 10 sectors gained, with education and health services adding 57,000, trade/transportation/utilities 36,000, professional and business services 11,000, construction and leisure/hospitality each 8,000
key_facts.excerpt: Education and health services again led with 57,000 hires, but trade, transportation and utilities added 36,000, professional and business services contributed 11,000 and construction and leisure and hospitality both rose by 8,000.

key_facts.fact: Information lost 9,000 jobs and natural resources/mining shed 3,000
key_facts.excerpt: Information -9,000... Natural resources/mining -3,000

key_facts.fact: Companies with fewer than 50 employees led with 67,000 hires, large employers (500+) added 40,000, and medium-sized firms contributed 17,000
key_facts.excerpt: Companies with fewer than 50 employees led with 67,000 new hires while those with 500 or more added 40,000 and medium-sized firms contributed 17,000.

key_facts.fact: Year-over-year pay growth for job-stayers held steady at 4.4%; pay growth for job-changers slowed slightly to 6.5% from 6.6% in April
key_facts.excerpt: Year-over-year pay growth for job-stayers was steady at 4.4 percent. For job-changers, the pace of growth slowed slightly, to 6.5 percent from 6.6 percent in April.

key_facts.fact: April private payrolls were revised down from 109,000 to 105,000
key_facts.excerpt: The April total number of jobs added was revised from 109,000 to 105,000.
